description.en:
A series of illustrated biographies intended to help Chinese children learn the works of famous poets studied in elementary and middle schools by presenting each poem within a comic based on the author's life circumstances around that particular poem's creation.


**Author's own word on the books**

Poetry is a key topic in Chinese language exams. When I was a child, I learned poems by rote memorization and never really understood what the poets were trying to express. My exam results depended entirely on how well I could recall them that day. It was only after I grew up—reading poets’ biographies and scholars’ papers—that I gradually understood the true meaning of the poems, felt their beauty, and genuinely felt proud of our cultural heritage.

But as a child, learning poetry was truly painful! So I asked myself: Is there any way to help young readers learn poetry more easily and joyfully, while also understanding its true meaning and experiencing its beauty?

After reading a great many books and papers on poetry and thinking about it every day, I finally discovered a solution:

1. Depict the poets as lively, adorable animals (for example, Li Bai as a free-spirited Arctic wolf; Meng Haoran as a countryside-loving white rabbit).

2. Render the poets’ life stories as engaging comics (for instance, Li Bai learned to read at age 5, studied the “Hundred Schools” at age 10, attended school on Mount Kuang at 18, apprenticed at 19, set out travelling at 20, married in at-marriage at 27, arrived in Chang’an at 30, had his audience with the emperor at 42, first met Du Fu in Luoyang at 44, was imprisoned in palace struggles at 57, and was released by the emperor at 59… All events are based on scholarly research, not fabrications or online encyclopedias).

3. Place each poem in the period of Li Bai’s life when it was composed (for example, at 27—when he married into the family—he wrote “Raising my head, I gaze at the bright moon; lowering it, I think of home.” At 31—when his job hunt in Chang’an failed—he wrote, “Sometime I’ll ride the wind and cleave the waves, setting my cloud-like sail to cross the boundless sea.” At 59—when he was freed—he wrote, “The gibbons’ cries on both banks never cease; a light boat has already passed ten thousand mountains.”).

Thus was born our “Animal Poetry Town” series. The first three volumes feature, respectively, the “Immortal of Poetry” Li Bai, the “Saint of Poetry” Du Fu, and the “Buddha of Poetry” Wang Wei.

Source: [https://zh.wikifur.com/wiki/诗词动物城：漫画李白传](https://zh.wikifur.com/wiki/诗词动物城：漫画李白传)

description.en:
Ye Zhen suffers from pluviophobia—a rare condition where every time it rains, her memories reset to one year ago, back to the day she made a promise with a certain man.
To uncover the truth behind her fragmented memories, she becomes entangled with Jiang An, the mysterious owner of a bookstore.

Cold, distant, and full of lies and secrets, Jiang An nevertheless seems to watch over Ye Zhen at every moment. His familiar face unsettles her even more—why does he look so much like someone she once knew?

But who is he, really?

description.en: For Li Zhiyan, the past is not merely a memory; it is an open wound stained with the purple hue of destruction. Having survived the devastation of her home as a child, she has turned her pain into armor and solitude into her only ally. Yet, when a battle awakens the ghosts of her childhood, she realizes that survivor's guilt is too heavy a burden to bear alone.
description.es: Para Li Zhiyan, el pasado no es solo un recuerdo; es una herida abierta teñida del color morado de la destrucción. Tras sobrevivir a la devastación de su hogar cuando era una niña, ha convertido su dolor en una armadura y la soledad en su única aliada. Sin embargo, cuando una batalla despierta los fantasmas de su infancia, se da cuenta de que la culpa de los supervivientes pesa demasiado para cargarla en solitario.

description.en: The reckless departure of the young Yue Tan, the mysterious unsealing of the "people in the paintings", the gradual awakenings of supernatural beings... The fetters between the millennium old demon spirit and Yue Tan is far more than just a simple contract. Lurking behind the scenes of an ordinary life hides a tremendous truth about parallel universes. Only by entering their story can you find the truth about life's origin and it's end.
